STEP 1 - Vessel type: The vessel is a square white plate. It has a rim band and a flat centre with no inner wall or shadow, so it is a flat plate (square).

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type cue: a square plate of this kind is typically 20-30 cm. This one looks medium, around 25 cm.
b) Reference cue: the plate spans roughly the length of the greens cluster plus the potato pieces. The potato chunks are about 3-4 cm each, and the plate width is about 7 to 8 of these chunk lengths across, which gives roughly 25 cm.
Reconciled width: about 25 cm square, area about 625 cm².

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Cooked potato/squash chunks (golden fried cubes plus a few dark roasted pieces): they cover roughly 12% of the plate area, about 75 cm². Thickness is about two chunks stacked at the thickest point, roughly 3 cm, averaging about 1.5 cm. Volume ≈ 110 ml. Density 0.6 g/ml for chopped vegetables gives about 65 g.
- Wilted/raw-looking greens (rocket or arugula with a light dressing): they cover about 25% of the plate, about 155 cm². The mound averages about 2 cm thick. Volume ≈ 310 ml. Cooked leafy greens at 0.6 g/ml gives about 185 g. Raw greens would be lighter, but this looks wilted and dressed, so I use the cooked density.
- Small garnish (a few pale onion or garlic bits and a little nut): negligible, a few grams.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: There is no visible base layer of rice or grains. The greens sit directly on the plate, so no hidden layer is added beyond the chunks already counted.

STEP 5 - Energy density as served:
- Roasted potato/squash with oil: about 120 kcal per 100 g.
- Dressed wilted greens: about 60 kcal per 100 g (includes oil from dressing).
- Garnish: about 150 kcal per 100 g, weight a few grams, so negligible.

Totals: potato/squash about 78 kcal; greens about 111 kcal; garnish about 5 kcal. The whole meal is roughly 250 g and about 195 kcal.
